data.note:
Reflection: I called Microtubule destabilizers (p=0.62), truth is Eg5 inhibitors — incorrect.

What happened: all 4 wells had strong mitotic arrest (high tubulin mean/std, high DNA, low solidity, rounded bright mitotics) and NSC voted 4/4 destabilizer with 10/10 neighbours of that class. I used that as prior and stayed with it. Both Eg5 inhibition and tubulin depolymerization produce sparse fields with condensed chromosomes and bright rounded mitotics at this resolution, so cosine similarity to destabilizer references was misleadingly high.

The microscopist twice flagged the discriminating detail I underweighted: spread interphase cells retained dense bright radial networks, and e5 explicitly proposed Eg5 inhibitors with monopolar spindles plus e16 favored preserved/bundled networks over diffuse depolymerization. I recalibrated 0.85 to 0.62 but did not flip.

Lesson: for mitotic arrests, require spindle-polarity / interphase filament-loss scoring before accepting NSC; preserved interphase microtubules + mitotic arrest should promote Eg5/stabilizer over destabilizer.

Literature for dossier: Eg5 inhibition causes monopolar spindle mitotic arrest (PMID:19351824 on Eg5 inhibitor-induced death; PMID:28392145 on Eg5-mediated mitotic arrest; PMID:34958711 on Eg5 inhibitor control of mitosis; PMID:31679979 on monopolar spindle induction); Eg5-independent spindle mechanisms complicate low-res reads (PMID:27354041). Reference check: vincristine CID5978 is ChEMBL tubulin inhibitor, explaining the atlas pull.

reflection.text:
I correctly detected a potent mitotic-arrest signature across all four wells: lower density with very high tub_glcm_contrast z=+40.2, tub_mean/std z~+17 to +28, high nuc_dna_integrated z=+19.8 and very low nuc_solidity. The unanimous atlas vote of Microtubule destabilizers 4/4 and 10/10 neighbours plus tub_mean dose-response rho=+1.00 drove the call to 0.85, later 0.62.

That quantitative vote misled me because bright condensed tubulin and rounded low-solidity nuclei are shared by destabilizers, stabilizers and Eg5 inhibitors at this resolution. Eg5 inhibition produces monopolar spindles and mitotic arrest that can mimic destabilizer brightness (PMID 31679979, PMID 19351824, PMID 28392145). I discounted the discriminating microscopist evidence in e5 that spread interphase cells retained filamentous radial microtubules with no complete depolymerization, which directly contradicts destabilizer filament loss, and I treated e5 listing Eg5 inhibitors as just one of three alternatives.

My acquisition choice compounded this by sampling four doses along the same mitotic axis instead of a discriminating morphology test, and only the review-requested low-dose interphase scoring in e16 forced attention to preserved bright networks. I recalibrated only to 0.62 and still kept the NSC prior on top instead of promoting Eg5 when interphase preservation plus mitotic arrest is its classic pattern.
what_was_right: Detected consistent mitotic-arrest phenotype across 0.003-1 uM: low density, high tubulin mean/std/contrast, high DNA content, low nuclear solidity.
Kept Eg5, stabilizer and Aurora alternatives after e5 and used frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 to correctly deprioritize Aurora polyploidy.
Recalibrated down from 0.85 to 0.62 after review-requested e16 showed preserved bright interphase networks contradicting destabilizer depolymerization.
what_was_wrong: Over-weighted repeated NSC 4/4 and 10/10 neighbour votes based on generic mitotic features shared with stabilizers and Eg5 inhibitors.
Misread increased tub_mean/std/contrast as destabilizer-specific when Eg5 monopolar spindles are also bright and textured at low resolution.
Discounted e5's specific contradiction: spread interphase cells retained filamentous radial microtubules with no complete depolymerization.
Sampled four dose levels on the same dose-response axis (tub_mean rho=+1.00) instead of early targeted scoring of spindle polarity and interphase filament loss versus preservation/bundling.

Small-molecule inhibition of mitotic kinesin Eg5 induces mitotic arrest and cell death.
